title: The Diagnostic Detour
lede: How long women wait for a diagnosis, how often the first one is wrong, and how that compares to men, for conditions that disproportionately affect women. Every figure is graded by source strength.

source_type_scale.registry: National health registry or population database
source_type_scale.survey: Patient self-report survey, often of advocacy-group members
source_type_scale.review: Systematic review or meta-analysis; see notes for underlying source types
source_type_scale.secondary: News, advocacy or company page citing a figure without a primary source

measures.time_to_diagnosis: Time from symptom onset (or first visit) to diagnosis, or age at diagnosis where noted
measures.misdiagnosis_rate: Share receiving a wrong initial diagnosis
measures.common_misdiagnosis: Share receiving a specific wrong label
measures.sex_difference: Women vs. men on the same measure
measures.psychosomatic_attribution: Share told symptoms were psychological, stress or over-concern

findings.unit: diagnoses of 1,369 where age at first hospital diagnosis differs by sex
findings.source_title: Population-wide analysis of differences in disease progression patterns in men and women (Westergaard et al., Nature Communications)
findings.notes: Age at first hospital diagnosis, not symptom-to-diagnosis delay. Abstract: age at first diagnosis is typically lower for men.

findings.unit: disease types diagnosed later in women
findings.source_title: Westergaard et al. (University of Copenhagen press summary)
findings.notes: From the press release, derived from supplementary data; not in the paper's abstract.

findings.unit: years later at diagnosis in women
findings.source_title: Westergaard et al. (press summary)
findings.notes: Partly confounded by sex-specific cancer mix.

findings.unit: years later at diagnosis in women
findings.source_title: Westergaard et al. (press summary)
findings.notes: From press release.

findings.unit: percent with a different initial diagnosis (168,534 of 564,412)
findings.source_title: Impact of initial hospital diagnosis on mortality for acute myocardial infarction: a national cohort study (Wu et al., Eur Heart J Acute Cardiovasc Care)
findings.notes: Misdiagnosed patients had about 70% higher 30-day mortality.

findings.unit: percent greater odds of initial misdiagnosis in women
findings.source_title: Wu et al.

findings.unit: percent greater odds of initial misdiagnosis in women
findings.source_title: Wu et al.

findings.unit: percent higher chance of initial misdiagnosis in women (overall)
findings.source_title: British Heart Foundation news
findings.notes: BHF states this came from additional analysis that was not published. Widely repeated. Do not headline; cite 59% and 41% instead.

findings.unit: years later at first ADHD record in females
findings.population: Sweden, Stockholm County, all residents 2011–2021; 37,591 females with ADHD record
findings.source_title: Time after time: failure to identify and support females with ADHD (Skoglund et al., J Child Psychol Psychiatry)
findings.notes: 95% CI 3.74–4.11. Includes children, so not adult-only. Females had more psychiatric comorbidity and healthcare use before diagnosis.

findings.unit: years, mean age at diagnosis
findings.source_title: Skoglund et al.
findings.notes: SD 13.8; median 19.0 (IQR 13.0–32.0). Age at diagnosis, not delay from onset.

findings.unit: years, mean age at diagnosis
findings.source_title: Skoglund et al.

findings.unit: years later at diagnosis in women (28.96 vs 24.13)
findings.population: Spain, 900 adults newly diagnosed at a specialist ADHD unit
findings.source_title: Sex differences in adults with ADHD: a population-based study (Amoretti et al., European Psychiatry)
findings.notes: p<0.001; no sex difference in age at symptom onset.

findings.unit: EUR per year, net cost vs matched controls, before diagnosis
findings.population: Denmark, national registers, OSA patients aged 20–64 diagnosed 2002–2019
findings.source_title: Long-term welfare consequences of sleep apnea in 20–64-year-olds – influence of gender (Jennum et al., Sleep)
findings.notes: 2020 prices; direct health and social welfare costs. The only sex-split, payer-grade pre-diagnosis cost figure found.

findings.unit: EUR per year, net cost vs matched controls, before diagnosis
findings.source_title: Jennum et al.

findings.unit: weeks, median, sicca onset to diagnosis
findings.population: Taiwan, National Health Insurance claims, population-based
findings.source_title: Diagnostic delay in patients with primary Sjögren's syndrome: a population-based cohort study in Taiwan (Healthcare)
findings.notes: IQR 30–208 weeks.

findings.unit: weeks, median
findings.source_title: Taiwan Sjögren's claims study
findings.notes: IQR 12–182 weeks.

findings.unit: outpatient visits, median
findings.source_title: Taiwan Sjögren's claims study
findings.notes: IQR 1–8; men median 2 (IQR 1–5). The only claims-based visit count found.

findings.unit: years longer median delay in women (5 vs 3)
findings.source_title: Sex differences in PROMs and clinical parameters in Sjögren's disease (Semin Arthritis Rheum)
findings.notes: p=0.008; women had symptom onset at median 37 vs 51 years.

findings.unit: years, mean (median 2)
findings.source_title: Impact of time to diagnosis in primary Sjögren's syndrome (Clin Exp Rheumatol)
findings.notes: Mean heavily skewed by a long tail; median is 2 years.

findings.unit: years, mean
findings.population: USA, AARDA member survey 2017, n=1,423 (1,287 women)
findings.source_title: AARDA Survey Study, 1996–2017 summary report
findings.notes: Earlier waves (women only): 5.4 yrs (1996), 4 (2001), 4 (2006), 3.5 (2013). Self-selected advocacy membership. The widely quoted 4.6 years matches no wave.

findings.unit: physicians, mean
findings.source_title: AARDA Survey Study
findings.notes: Men 3.00; overall 3.95. 1996 wave: 6.02 physicians.

findings.unit: percent told they were overly concerned about their health
findings.source_title: AARDA Survey Study

findings.unit: percent reporting a psychosomatic misdiagnosis
findings.population: International online survey, Dec 2024–Mar 2025, n=6,607 (91.2% female, 69.7% UK)
findings.source_title: Sex and disease differences in patients' diagnostic experiences in autoimmune diseases (Sloan et al., eClinicalMedicine)
findings.notes: Men 22%; aOR 1.74. Figures taken from press coverage; verify against the paper.

findings.unit: percent reporting a psychiatric misdiagnosis
findings.source_title: Sloan et al.
findings.notes: Men 33%; aOR 1.46. Autoimmune thyroid disease was the most common primary condition (22.9%).

findings.unit: percent waiting 4 or more years
findings.source_title: Sloan et al.
findings.notes: Men 26%. Modal delay: men under 3 months, women 1–2 years.

findings.unit: months, median, onset to diagnosis
findings.population: Spain, multicenter prospective cohort, 190 newly diagnosed IBD patients
findings.source_title: Gender biases and diagnostic delay in inflammatory bowel disease (Sempere et al., Inflamm Bowel Dis)
findings.notes: IQR 3.7–31; p=.008 vs men.

findings.unit: months, median
findings.source_title: Sempere et al.

findings.unit: months, median
findings.source_title: Sempere et al.

findings.unit: percent with at least one misdiagnosis before IBD (117 of 190)
findings.source_title: Sempere et al.

findings.unit: month longer median latency in women (6 vs 5), not significant
findings.source_title: Sex disparities in treatment trajectories of IBD are associated with diagnostic delay (Blüthner et al., Crohn's & Colitis 360)
findings.notes: p=0.490. Counter-evidence to the Spanish cohort.

findings.unit: years, mean, first symptoms to diagnosis (median 4)
findings.population: Sweden, Swedish Society for Coeliacs members, 818 with symptom-delay data
findings.source_title: Delay to celiac disease diagnosis and its implications for health-related quality of life (Norström et al., BMC Gastroenterol)
findings.notes: Median 4 years (quartiles 1–14). Primary source of the widely cited 9.7 years.

findings.unit: years, mean, first doctor visit to diagnosis (median 1)
findings.source_title: Norström et al.
findings.notes: Median 1 year (quartiles 0–8). Most diagnosed quickly; a long tail is not.

findings.unit: percent with delay over 10 years; female sex associated with prolonged delay
findings.source_title: Factors associated with long diagnostic delay in celiac disease (Fuchs et al., Scand J Gastroenterol)
findings.notes: 261 of 825 over 10 years. Effect size for sex not extracted.

findings.unit: years, range of mean delays across 17 studies
findings.population: 17 observational studies 2018–2023; UK, USA, Australia, Germany, France, Italy, Canada, NZ
findings.source_title: Time to diagnose endometriosis: a systematic literature review (De Corte et al., BJOG)
findings.notes: Underlying: cohorts and surveys. UK 5.5–8, USA 5–8, Australia 6.4–8. Delay mainly physician-driven.

findings.unit: years, average across studies (range 1.5–11.3)
findings.source_title: Understanding diagnostic delay for endometriosis: a scoping review (Fryer et al., Health Care Women Int)
findings.notes: Primary care presentation to diagnosis 2.9 years. Mixed underlying sources.

findings.unit: months, median
findings.population: Systematic review of quantitative studies, adults
findings.source_title: Factors associated with delay in the diagnosis and treatment of SLE in adult patients: a systematic review (Rheumatology)
findings.notes: IQR 0–32.3. Underlying: cohorts. The widely cited 'nearly six years' traces only to a Lupus Foundation patient survey.

findings.unit: months median in women vs 14.09 in men
findings.source_title: SLE diagnostic delay systematic review (Rheumatology)
findings.notes: Women IQR 1.1–144.0; men IQR 0.0–18.5.

findings.unit: months, mean
findings.source_title: Delayed diagnosis adversely affects outcome in SLE: cross sectional analysis of the LuLa cohort (Kernder et al., Lupus)
findings.notes: Self-reported; 13 months of this was onset to first physician visit.

findings.unit: physicians, average
findings.source_title: From first symptoms to diagnosis of SLE: mapping the journey of patients (Clin Exp Rheumatol)
findings.notes: Median total delay 24 months; only 28.4% diagnosed within 6 months.

findings.unit: years longer mean delay in women (8.8 vs 6.5)
findings.source_title: Understanding how the diagnostic delay of spondyloarthritis differs between women and men (Jovaní et al., J Rheumatol)
findings.notes: Meta-analysis of cohorts. Figures via secondary summary; verify in full text.

findings.unit: percent of women correctly diagnosed at first visit, vs 30% of men
findings.source_title: The impact of gender and sex on diagnosis, treatment outcomes and HRQoL in axSpA
findings.notes: Women more often first labelled fibromyalgia.

findings.unit: weeks longer median GP referral delay in women (10 vs 3)
findings.population: Norway, one year of referrals to a rheumatology unit
findings.source_title: Women with early rheumatoid arthritis are referred later than men (Palm & Purinszky, Ann Rheum Dis)
findings.notes: Total lag 16 weeks for both sexes. Leiden cohort: gap eliminated after 2000. May not reflect current practice.

findings.unit: years (women 5.10 vs men 5.03, onset to diagnosis)
findings.source_title: Quantitative effect of sex on disease activity and disability accumulation in MS (Magyari & Koch-Henriksen, J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry)
findings.notes: No meaningful sex gap; the paper reports diagnostic delay did not differ significantly by sex. The exact 5.10/5.03 figures came via trade press; confirm in the full text. Include as counter-evidence.

findings.unit: percent of women diagnosed before tertiary referral, vs 57.0% of men
findings.population: Germany, Charité tertiary headache centre, 1,130 patients
findings.source_title: Sex-related disparities in migraine recognition and management (J Headache Pain)
findings.notes: OR 0.47 for men. Men, not women, are under-recognized here. Include as counter-evidence.

findings.unit: months, median, first physician visit to diagnosis
findings.population: International online survey with Dysautonomia International, n=4,835
findings.source_title: The face of postural tachycardia syndrome (Shaw et al., J Intern Med)
findings.notes: IQR 6–72 months. Mean 4.7±6.9 years.

findings.unit: years mean in women vs 3.0 in men
findings.source_title: Shaw et al.

findings.unit: percent told symptoms were psychiatric or psychological before diagnosis
findings.source_title: Shaw et al.
findings.notes: Repeated by secondary sites; confirm in the paper's Table 3 before publishing.

findings.unit: years longer mean delay in women (7.0 vs 3.8)
findings.population: Australia, Adelaide specialist clinic registry, 500 people, 2021–2024
findings.source_title: Symptom burden, quality of life, and diagnostic journey of people with POTS (Med J Aust)
findings.notes: p=0.010; 25.5% delayed over 10 years. Single-clinic registry, graded cohort.

findings.unit: percent who saw more than 10 doctors
findings.population: Dysautonomia International survey, over 700 POTS patients, Dec 2013
findings.source_title: Diagnostic Delay in POTS (Dysautonomia International)
findings.notes: Mean delay reported as 5 years 11 months. Advocacy-run survey.

findings.unit: years, mean, symptom onset to diagnosis, for those diagnosed in 2020 (median 12.0)
findings.population: USA, You + ME Registry participants with clinician diagnosis
findings.source_title: Time from symptom onset to ME/CFS diagnosis: 1987 to 2022 (Solve M.E.)
findings.notes: Foundation-run patient registry, self-report. No sex split.

findings.unit: percent who waited more than 5 years
findings.population: UK, ME Association website survey 2016, n=656
findings.source_title: Diagnosis of ME/CFS: the importance of having an early and accurate diagnosis (ME Association)
findings.notes: Only 18% diagnosed within 6 months. No sex split.

findings.unit: percent offered antidepressants instead of HRT as first treatment
findings.population: UK, Newson Health clinic survey, sample size for this figure not stated
findings.source_title: Newson Health clinic survey (posted 17 Feb 2025, not peer-reviewed)
findings.notes: Clinic-run survey with a commercial interest in HRT. Use only with that label.

findings.unit: percent already on antidepressants at first menopause-clinic visit (172 of 920)
findings.population: UK, largest specialist menopause clinic, retrospective cohort
findings.source_title: Glynne, Kamal, McColl, Newson, Reisel et al., Br J Psychiatry
findings.notes: 49.4% of those had never used HRT. Authors are clinic staff; self-selected sample; conflict-of-interest flag.

findings.unit: percent of women aged 40–64 on SSRIs
findings.source_title: Rochester Epidemiology Project SSRI prevalence
findings.notes: Highest of any age-sex group. Prevalence only; says nothing about appropriateness.

gaps.note: No primary delay, visit-count or sex-split figures found.
No sex-disaggregated delay or misdiagnosis figures; only qualitative work.

No study measures how often perimenopause-attributed symptoms turn out to be thyroid, autoimmune, iron-deficiency or cardiovascular. This is the thesis's central evidence hole and a study Herada could run on claims or EHR data.

gaps.condition: Fibromyalgia, PCOS, ovarian cancer, EDS, bipolar-as-unipolar, autism in adult women

untraceable.claim: 4.6 years and 4.8 doctors to an autoimmune diagnosis (AARDA)
untraceable.note: Matches no wave of AARDA's own survey report. Use wave-specific figures.

untraceable.claim: Over $10,000 per year in unnecessary pre-diagnosis spend for autoimmune patients
untraceable.note: No primary study found. Do not use.

untraceable.claim: Women 50% more likely to be misdiagnosed after a heart attack
untraceable.note: BHF says this came from unpublished analysis. Cite 59% (STEMI) and 41% (NSTEMI).

untraceable.claim: Lupus takes nearly six years to diagnose
untraceable.note: Traces only to a Lupus Foundation of America patient survey. Published medians are 18–24 months.
A 2012 foundation baseline; the foundation now says 3 years, and claims data show about 2 years median.

headline.text: Across hundreds of diseases, women are older than men at first diagnosis
